title: Oxygen — Passenger Oxygen Duration and Cabin Altitude Limitations
abstract: Flight crew limitation on passenger oxygen duration and on the cabin altitude profile that must be achieved after a depressurisation, stated as one figure for the whole fleet.

sections.purpose: This entry states the passenger oxygen duration limitation and the cabin altitude profile the crew must achieve after a depressurisation.
sections.description: Passenger oxygen is supplied by chemical generators in the passenger service units. A generator starts when the mask is pulled and runs for a fixed duration that cannot be stopped, extended or restarted. That duration determines the descent profile the crew must fly: the cabin altitude has to be brought below the published level before the generators expire, and over high terrain the drift-down profile is what makes this a real constraint rather than a theoretical one. One generator duration is fitted throughout the fleet, so a single figure applies to every aircraft and the crew has nothing to look up. Route planning over high terrain is checked against that figure at the network level rather than aircraft by aircraft.
sections.crew_procedure: After a depressurisation, don the crew masks, establish communication and initiate the emergency descent. Fly the profile that brings the cabin altitude below the published level within the published oxygen duration. Over high terrain, fly the drift-down profile published for the route and confirm before departure that it is compatible with that duration.
sections.limitation_note: The maximum time at a cabin altitude above the published level is limited by the passenger oxygen duration. Dispatch on a route whose drift-down profile exceeds that duration is not permitted.

type_data.crew_action: Fly the descent profile that brings the cabin altitude below the published level within the fitted oxygen duration.

title: Oxygen — Passenger Oxygen Duration and Cabin Altitude Limitations

issue.reason: The revised duration limitation is given an effectivity that follows the aircraft configuration record rather than a fleet date.

abstract: Flight crew limitation on passenger oxygen duration and the cabin altitude profile after a depressurisation, with two durations in service and the applicable figure taken from the aircraft configuration record.

sections.purpose: This entry states the passenger oxygen duration limitation and the cabin altitude profile the crew must achieve after a depressurisation.
sections.description: Passenger oxygen is supplied by chemical generators in the passenger service units. A generator starts when the mask is pulled and runs for a fixed duration that cannot be stopped, extended or restarted. The duration fitted to the aircraft determines the descent profile the crew must fly: the cabin altitude has to be brought below the published level before the generators expire, and the drift-down profile over high terrain is what makes that a real constraint rather than a theoretical one. Two durations are in service across the fleet. Aircraft at the longer duration standard may be planned on routes that aircraft at the shorter standard may not, and the aircraft standard is stated on the load sheet. Generators of different durations are never mixed in one cabin, so a single figure always applies to the whole aircraft.
sections.crew_procedure: After a depressurisation, don the crew masks, establish communication and initiate the emergency descent. Fly the profile that brings the cabin altitude below the published level within the oxygen duration fitted to the aircraft. Over high terrain, fly the drift-down profile published for the route and confirm before departure that it is compatible with the oxygen duration fitted.
sections.limitation_note: The maximum time at a cabin altitude above the published level is limited by the passenger oxygen duration fitted to the aircraft, which is stated on the load sheet. Dispatch on a route whose drift-down profile exceeds that duration is not permitted. Generators of different durations must not be mixed in one cabin. The change from the shorter to the longer figure is effective per aircraft, not per fleet and not on a calendar date: it applies from the moment the aircraft configuration record shows the conversion complete, which is the day the last generator in that cabin is swapped. Until that entry exists the shorter figure governs, whatever the campaign plan says.

type_data.crew_action: Fly the descent profile that brings the cabin altitude below the published level within the fitted oxygen duration.
